added_failures_note: The reviewed run was suite-unarmed, so its manifest carries neither baseline_suite nor after_suite. The count is derived from the run's own gate logs: logs/head-suite.log (revision 235fe8b1e7) and logs/base-suite.log (revision c2e2d17f) each report 2 failed, 174 passed with the same two ids (test_no_removal_site_still_deletes_with_git_worktree_remove under tests/test_a_worktree_release_is_whole.py, test_no_removal_path_decides_liveness_from_the_phase_gated_claim under tests/test_every_removal_path_reads_the_wide_claim.py), so the head added no failing test. The two committing failures reproduce at the base revision and are not this node's.

findings.text: The new test file defines its own _git helper instead of importing tests/helpers/git.py:12 git(), which 163 test files already import. The owner is not merely equivalent: it strips RUN_ID_ENV from the child environment because the git shim refuses a mutating verb whose run's live pointer it cannot read, which is exactly the state a test is in after naming a temporary configuration home. The local copy reproduces that refusal hazard for the git init/add/commit calls at lines 64-90, so the test can fail inside a worker where the shared helper would pass.

This assertion compares the release stored in the record against the same RELEASE constant the test handed to _record_release_on_ledger, so its two sides move together and it holds for any code that round-trips its input. It is not vacuous (a missing or mutated release fails), but the guard against the write not committing rests on the independent assertions at lines 176, 180 and 183, not on this one.
